articles.headline: Man arrested on stalking charges at LeBron James' home in Los Angeles
articles.description: A man was arrested on Friday night at LeBron James' Brentwood, California, home, a Los Angeles Police Department spokesperson confirmed to ESPN on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ロサンゼルスのレブロン・ジェームズの自宅でストーキング容疑の男を逮捕
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス市警察の広報担当者が土曜日にESPNに語ったところによると、金曜日の夜、カリフォルニア州ブレントウッドにあるレブロン・ジェームズの自宅で男が逮捕された。
articles.body:
A man was arrested Friday night at LeBron James' Brentwood, California, home, a Los Angeles Police Department spokesperson confirmed to ESPN on Saturday.

LAPD officers responded to a call at 9:39 p.m. Friday to investigate a possible burglary on James' property, the spokesperson said.

A suspect was apprehended at the residence, taken into custody and booked for stalking, the spokesperson said.

James was in Cleveland on Friday night for his Philadelphia 76ers' game against the Cavaliers. The Sixers lost 119-95 to his former team.

A representative for James had no comment about the incident.

articles.headline: Sources: Saints to activate WR Jordyn Tyson, LT Kelvin Banks
articles.description: Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. will be active against the Browns on Sunday, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：セインツ、WRジョーディン・タイソンとLTケルビン・バンクスをアクティブ登録へ
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、セインツの新人ワイドレシーバーであるジョーディン・タイソンと、レフトタックルのケルビン・バンクスJr.が日曜日のブラウンズ戦で出場可能になる。
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. will be active against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Saturday.

Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, is set to make his debut after injuring his hamstring in August. He returned to practice for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in a joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 13.

He was listed as questionable on the injury report along with Banks, who also returned to practice following surgery on his ankle.

Tyson was expected to be out at least two months after the hamstring injury, which occurred after he landed awkwardly after catching a pass.

Both Tyson and the Saints said the injury was not related to his previous hamstring issues from college; he missed three games for Arizona State last year.

He also tore his ACL, MCL and PCL in his left knee when he was at Colorado in 2022, fractured his collarbone in 2024 and sprained his ankle that caused him to miss spring practices in 2025.

Tyson said he feels like the extended time to get himself right has been "a blessing."

"Kind of got a slow start to the NFL, so I got to kind of take my time and kind of really adjust to it," he said.

A source said the Saints released running back Kendre Miller as a corresponding move upon activating Tyson off injured reserve.

Miller, a 2023 third-round pick out of TCU, led the team's struggling run game with 159 yards this season. The Saints released him after claiming running back Audric Estime off waivers from the Browns. Estime was with the team last year and in camp but was waived with an injury settlement.

The Saints rushed for only 18 yards in their last game before the bye week.

articles.headline: Nottingham Forest condemn Man City to 3rd straight Premier League loss
articles.description: Nottingham Forest condemned Manchester City to a third straight Premier League loss as Enzo Maresca's previously unbeaten side slipped further behind leaders Arsenal.
articles.headlineJa: ノッティンガム・フォレスト、マンチェスター・シティにプレミアリーグ3連敗を喫させる
articles.descriptionJa: エンツォ・マレスカ率いる無敗のチームが首位アーセナルからさらに引き離される中、ノッティンガム・フォレストがマンチェスター・シティにプレミアリーグ3連敗を喫させた。
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest condemned Manchester City to a third straight Premier League loss as Enzo Maresca's side slipped further behind leaders Arsenal.

Despite starting the day in the Premier League's relegation zone, Forest triumphed 3-1 at the City Ground thanks to two goals from former City striker Liam Delap.

It is the first time in two years that City have lost three straight in the league and the first time they have conceded three goals to a team that begun the day in the Premier League's bottom three since September 2019.

City, who won seven straight games to start the season, remain in second place but are now six points behind leaders and title holders Arsenal.

The victory took Forest out of the relegation zone and sent Manchester United into the bottom three.

It could be a coming of age for both Delap and Forest, who had struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games.

Delap had scored once in his opening eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double suggested he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season.

Delap began his career at City, but played just two Premier League games for the club.

City found themselves 2-0 down inside 20 minutes and trailed at halftime in a third consecutive Premier League game for the fist time since 2007, before the cub was taken over by Abu Dhabi United Group.

Jair Cunha scored Forest's opening goal, while City briefly threatened a comeback when Rayan Cherki scored early in the second half.

City's slump in form comes amid the backdrop of the ongoing appeal against Premier League charges, their season is showing signs of falling apart.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: VAR controversy ignites Elland Road as Leeds bring Tottenham back down to earth
articles.description: Tottenham's unbeaten run was ended at Leeds but do Roberto De Zerbi's side have a right to be aggrieved with the officials? ESPN's Tom Chambers reports from Elland Road.
articles.headlineJa: リーズがトッテナムの勢いを止める、エランド・ロードではVARを巡る論争が勃発
articles.descriptionJa: トッテナムの無敗記録はリーズによって断たれたが、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームには審判に対して不満を抱く権利があるのだろうか？ESPNのトム・チェンバースがエランド・ロードから報告する。
articles.body:
LEEDS, England - You could have forgiven Roberto De Zerbi if he had burst through the door of the Elland Road media suite, howling about officiating injustice and hinting at conspiracy.

It's a tactic employed by plenty of his peers after a troubling defeat, such as this one was for Tottenham Hotspur in West Yorkshire. Instead, the Italian solemnly walked through the side door and sat to patiently field questions. There was no wide-eyed outburst to clip up, no raging against the dying of the light. Saturday's match was decided by Noah Okafor's 79th-minute strike past Antonín Kinsky, 97 seconds after his introduction off the bench, but it hinged on referee John Brooks and VAR Tony Harrington deciding against sending off Jayden Bogle after half an hour.

"I can't say something more because I didn't see clearly the situation," De Zerbi said as he went on to express "surprise" at the decision but not much more, focusing instead on his own team's shortcomings.

He added to TNT Sports: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision, I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where we can improve."

Bogle's coming together with Mathys Tel in front of the dugouts was unusual in that it was his left foot which made contact with the Spurs winger's ankle while he tried to get in position to make a tackle with his right. It's the sort of incident that is framed by different verbs, depending on your allegiance. Those of a Leeds persuasion would temper emotions with words like 'clumsy' and 'accidental.' While Spurs' fanbase would describe it as 'ugly' and 'dangerous.'

Spurs midfielder Xavi Simons put himself firmly in the latter camp on Saturday evening as he went on Instagram to compare the Bogle-Tel incident with the red card he was shown against Liverpool last season for an admittedly similar offence. Leeds boss Daniel Farke was perhaps over-wrought in the defence of his player as he described Bogle as "a butterfly" and "probably the softest player in the whole league," surely creating a new nickname for the defender within the Leeds dressing room in the process.

Whatever the correct interpretation of the incident, after the officials had sided with Leeds' version of events, pointing to "a lack of speed going into the challenge", this match proved unwinnable for De Zerbi's men.

- Leeds 1-0 Tottenham: Okafor strike ends Spurs, De Zerbi's winning run 

- De Zerbi questions Leeds-Spurs refereeing, Farke says Bogle 'my butterfly' 

Elland Road had been sleepy during the tepid opening exchanges of this Saturday lunchtime kick-off with the Leeds fans roused only momentarily by a VAR check for a possible handball in the box by Mateus Fernandes. The Bogle-Tel collision that followed gave them a moment of perceived injustice to rail against as they lambasted the Frenchman for what they felt was an example of a visiting player making too much out of an innocuous tackle. articles.headline: Man City slip to third straight defeat as Liam Delap inspires Nottingham Forest
articles.description: Liam Delap's emphatic brace earned Nottingham Forest a first home win of the season and piled the misery on Manchester City with a 3-1 victory.
articles.headlineJa: リアム・デラップがノッティンガム・フォレストを牽引、マンチェスター・シティは3連敗に陥る
articles.descriptionJa: リアム・デラップの決定的な2ゴールにより、ノッティンガム・フォレストは今シーズン初のホーム勝利を収め、3-1でマンチェスター・シティの苦境に追い打ちをかけた。
articles.body:
Liam Delap's emphatic brace earned Nottingham Forest a first home win of the season and piled the misery on Manchester City with a 3-1 victory.

Delap scored in either half after Jair Cunha had given Forest an early lead as City lost for the third Premier League game in a row.

This victory could be a coming of age for both Delap and Forest, who had struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games.

Delap had scored once in his opening eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double proved he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season.

The win is their first in the league at the City Ground since April and sends Manchester United into the bottom three. City found themselves 2-0 down inside 20 minutes, but did threaten a comeback when Rayan Cherki scored early in the second half.

But they slipped to a third loss on the bounce and amid the backdrop of the ongoing appeal against Premier League charges, their season is showing signs of falling apart.

Forest enjoyed an opening 20 minutes they could never have imagined as they were all over City and surged into a two-goal lead.

Having waited the best part of eight and a half hours to score in front of their fans, perhaps unsurprisingly the drought, going back to last May, was ended by an unlikely source in the sixth minute.

Centre-back Jair robbed Josko Gvardiol high up the pitch, advanced into the area and slotted past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

It was 2-0 in the 19th minute as Delap broke his City Ground duck in fine style.

Former Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, who had a nightmare return to the ground, and Iliman Ndiaye left the ball to each other in the Forest half and Delap pounced, running all the way into the City area before firing an unstoppable shot past Donnarumma.

James McAtee almost made it three soon after, but he skied an effort from 16 yards after Forest had again robbed City of possession.

The visitors were rattled and had a big repair job on their hands.

They should have got one back in the 25th minute as Marc Guehi's cross was perfect for Enzo Fernandez, who could not keep his header from six yards down.

Erling Haaland had been a virtual spectator but came alive in the 40th minute, only to be denied by some great defending by Jair.

Anderson's ball to Abdukodir Khusanov split the Forest defence and the right-back fed Haaland, who rounded goalkeeper Matz Sels but saw his shot heroically cleared off the line by Jair.

But they did get one back in the 52nd minute as Cherki delivered a firecracker.

Jeremy Doku was clear down the left and his cross was deflected into the path of the France international, who slammed a half-volley into the top corner from the edge of the area.

City smelled blood and Haaland was a whisker away from levelling when his curled effort from 12 yards went just over.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Arsenal robbed of a penalty through misapplied law
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグVAR解説：ルールの誤適用によりアーセナルがPKを奪われる
articles.descriptionJa: VARはしばしば議論を呼びますが、判定はどのように下されるのでしょうか？担当レフェリーのアンディ・デイビスが詳しく解説します。
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

Photo credit: USA Sports, NBC

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Arsenal robbed of a penalty

Arsenal 1-0 Hull City (Nov. 7)

Referee: Farai Hallam

VAR: Michael Oliver

Time: 42 minutes

Incident: Penalty not awarded to Arsenal for an offside offense.

What happened: Hull's Nobel Mendy appeared to grab the shirt of Kai Havertz as the Arsenal attacker attempted to get on the end of a ball into the box.

In a confusing twist and following a VAR review, Hallam explained to the stadium that a foul action had been committed by Mendy, but Havertz was in an offside position and therefore the decision was no penalty and a restart of an indirect free kick to Hull.

VAR decision: VAR recommended an on-field review for a possible penalty to Arsenal.

VAR review: Oliver asked Hallam to review the possible penalty to Arsenal at the pitchside monitor. Once at the screen, Hallam agreed that a foul had been committed by Mendy on Havertz, however he also determined that Havertz was in an offside position when the ball was played and therefore the outcome should be a defensive free kick to Hull and not a penalty to Arsenal.

Verdict: In a complex and confusing set of circumstances, the law was incorrectly applied in this incident by Hallam. A penalty should have been the outcome, and fortunately for him and ProRef, Arsenal went on to win the game, which will dampen any fallout from the situation.

What the law says: If a player in an offside position is fouled before or without committing an offside offense, the foul is to be penalized.

I have some sympathy for Hallam, as the judgment of when a player should be judged as impacting an opponent can be open to interpretation. The positioning of Havertz and the possibility of him impacting on Mendy's next action has clearly caused a misread of the situation with the referee applying the law incorrectly.

Between the referee, Oliver and his assistant VAR, the correct outcome should have been reached, and the "live comms" will be interesting when they are released. I have been a big advocate of "live comms" being available, and this is another incident when some much-needed clarity was needed in real time, which could easily have been communicated and explained.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's attacking struggles: Must stop chasing 'perfect goal'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal must stop trying to score "the perfect goal" after Saturday's narrow 1-0 win over Hull City.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタが語るアーセナルの攻撃の苦戦：「完璧なゴール」を追い求めるのをやめるべき
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のハル・シティ戦を1-0で辛勝した後、ミケル・アルテタは、アーセナルは「完璧なゴール」を狙おうとするのをやめなければならないと述べました。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said Arsenal must stop trying to score "the perfect goal" after Saturday's narrow 1-0 win over Hull City.

The Gunners struggled to break down their opponents in a game short on clear chances before captain Martin Ødegaard netted a 72nd-minute winner from close range.

Arsenal moved six points clear at the top of the Premier League after equalling their best-ever start to a season -- nine wins from 10 games -- and were later given more good news thanks to Manchester City's defeat to Nottingham Forest. But Arteta is eyeing further improvement after the international break having seen his team win eight matches across all competitions by a single-goal margin so far this season.

"[We need to] be more efficient," he said. "We are one against one against the keeper. That's happened twice today. There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing. So many shots that have been deflected, blocked. We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

"Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And open, I think, the scoreline much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.

"We had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that. And then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box, insisting, insisting and insisting until we are able to break them down. And this is exactly how we won the game."

Arteta also admitted he was left baffled by the VAR's decision not to award the Gunners a first-half penalty for a challenge on Kai Havertz.

- If Arsenal find attacking spark, they could run away with the league

- Ødegaard scores winner as Arsenal scrape past Hull to extend PL lead

- As it happened: Arsenal beat Hull City

Hull defender Nobel Mendy pulled Havertz's shirt in the box but he was in an offside position. Referee Farai Hallam was sent to the monitor and agreed Havertz had been fouled but then awarded Hull a free-kick.

The law states that a player hasn't committed an offside offence until he challenges an opponent for the ball, but there are past incidents where a penalty has been given and also not given for similar situations.

"I haven't watched it back and I didn't watch it back so I don't have to lie to you guys," Arteta said. "I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji [analyst Ben Chadwick] was telling me it's a clear penalty.

"So I heard now that they decided not to because of the starting position of Kai that he was offside. I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they will make that clear to understand it."

articles.headline: Premier League recap: Man City's fall at Forest sees Arsenal pull away in title race
articles.description: Another weekend of European soccer is underway, with Man City falling further behind the Premier League champions after Arsenal beat Hull City.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグまとめ：マン・シティがフォレストに敗れ、アーセナルが優勝争いでリードを広げる

articles.body:
It's the final weekend of European club action before the last international break of 2026!

We kicked things off in Yorkshire, where Leeds United beat Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 in Saturday's early Premier League clash.

Then, defending champions Arsenal defeated Hull City 1-0 at the Emirates, while across London Fulham and Newcastle United drew 1-1 at Craven Cottage. Finally, Nottingham Forest earned a resounding 3-1 victory over Manchester City to round off the day's Premier League action.

Plenty happened elsewhere across Europe, too, with newly crowned Ballon d'Or Harry Kane assisting both goals in Bayern Munich's 2-1 win at Mainz.

Relive all the action from Saturday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: Browns QB Deshaun Watson out of concussion protocol
articles.description: Browns QB Deshaun Watson is out of the concussion protocol, but he is questionable. Shedeur Sanders will get the start against the Saints.
articles.headlineJa: ブラウンズのQBデショーン・ワトソン、脳震盪プロトコルを通過
articles.descriptionJa: ブラウンズのQBデショーン・ワトソンは脳震盪プロトコルを通過しましたが、出場は不透明な状況です。セドゥア・サンダースがセインツ戦の先発を務めます。
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has cleared concussion protocol, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

Browns coach Todd Monken said Friday that Shedeur Sanders will get the start. It's unclear if Watson will serve as the backup or if that responsibility will fall to Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green.

Sanders has attempted just three passes this season in spot appearances during two games. He took all the starting reps in practice this week after Watson self-reported concussion symptoms Tuesday morning and was placed in the protocol.

As a rookie last season, Sanders made seven starts, completing 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He went 3-4 in those starts.

Cleveland (5-3) faces the Saints this week and then hosts the Houston Texans in Week 10 before entering their bye.

Information from ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi was used in this report.

articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Saturday

The NBA goes international today, as the Indiana Pacers and Denver Nuggets face off in Mexico City early this evening.

Indiana guard T.J. McConnell has a chance to make his season debut, while superstar Tyrese Haliburton remains sidelined with a hamstring injury. Denver, meanwhile, is looking to reclaim its identity as a contender.

The stateside portion of the schedule features six other games, headlined by a Western Conference showdown between the expectedly elite San Antonio Spurs and the impressively competitive Portland Trail Blazers. Portland has the statistical makeup (second in offense, 12th in defense) of a real contender. We'll learn about both teams in this marquee matchup.

Among Eastern contenders, the New York Knicks are seeking to go above .500 as they visit a Cleveland Cavaliers group that just dominated a surging Philadelphia 76ers squad last night. With Cleveland possibly missing Jarrett Allen for a second straight game, both Peyton Watson and a veteran forward we'll discuss below could emerge with meaningful roles.

A positive trend across today's slate is the presence of closer point spreads; only one of today's seven games sports a betting line above 7.5 points. This signals potential for competitive contests, which often result in more predictable playing time, usage and production patterns.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

 Mario Hezonja, SF, Cleveland Cavaliers (rostered in 6.6% of ESPN leagues)

This second chapter of Hezonja's NBA career has been fascinating. Returning as a physical presence in the paint and on the boards, Hezonja also flashes great footwork on defense and in transition, adding dimension to his impact in real and fantasy contexts. The Cavs might need big minutes from Hezonja on the second leg of a back-to-back with Allen likely out again.

 Tari Eason, SF/PG, Houston Rockets (18.8%)

The unintentional theme of today's endorsements is hustle. The names on today's pickup list find their work via hustle and grinding out possessions on both ends of the floor. Eason might be the epitome of the archetype, always willing to create havoc in passing lanes and crash the glass from Josh Hart-like angles. You won't be wowed by the scoring results, rather by a collection of turnovers and rebounds.

 Quenton Jackson, PG/SG, Indiana Pacers (6.6%)

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Kaelon Black and Malik Willis lead the way
articles.description: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール、直前の補強候補：ケーロン・ブラックとマリク・ウィリスが筆頭
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我やバイウィーク、厳しい対戦カードによってラインナップの調整が必要な場合は、マット・ボーエンが推奨する選択肢をリストアップしている。
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in under 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

Let's start the Week 9 list at the quarterback position with two players who have positive matchups (based on the numbers). After that, we will pivot to the wide receiver spot, and I've gone a little deeper than usual, with five pass catchers who bring stable floors to the lineup. I also have three running backs who can be played as flex in deeper leagues, plus a tight end who has quietly put together three straight weeks of quality production. As always, we'll end with D/ST, but it's pretty lean out there right now.

Quarterbacks

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (26.6% rostered; at Philadelphia Eagles)

McCarthy scored 10.18 points in Week 7, completing 20-of-28 for 252 yards. McCarthy failed to throw a touchdown, and the rushing totals were down (one carry, one yard), but he is seeing the field with speed and driving the ball from the pocket. With a matchup Sunday versus an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom 10 versus quarterbacks, McCarthy has value in superflex formats.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (18.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Willis is averaging 19.8 points over his past three games, with multiple touchdown throws in two of them. Plus, he brings a dual-threat element to the lineup as Willis is averaging 32.1 yards rushing this season with a touchdown in two of his past three games. Given Willis' rising numbers, he's a smart play this week versus a Lions defense that has allowed a league-worst 24.8 points per game to opposing quarterbacks.

Wide receivers

Malik Washington, Miami Dolphins (39.4% rostered; vs. Detroit Lions)

Washington scored a season-high 15 points in Week 8 as he caught his first touchdown of the season. He's now posted double-digit points in four of his past five games. With his route/alignment versatility, Washington will also see rushing attempts, and he gets a quality matchup versus a Lions defense that ranks in the bottom five versus wide receivers.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (44.3% rostered; vs. Dallas Cowboys)

I would take the matchup with Allen versus the Dallas defense Sunday. This Cowboys unit ranks in the bottom 10 versus wide receivers and Allen has scored 13 or more points in two of his past three games. The touchdown upside is limited with Allen, but he can still uncover and find space as an outlet. After catching all seven of his targets for 67 yards versus the Jaguars last week, Allen can be played as high-floor WR3.

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 9
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's ranks are here to help.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール 第9週フレックスおよびスーパーフレックス・ランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 今週、順位が僅差の選手たちの間でどちらにするか迷っていませんか？エリック・カラベルのランキングがその判断をサポートします。
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Jaguars-Ravens game.

Teams on bye in Week 9: Steelers, Titans

Week 9 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ MIA

It's hard for a RB to average 28 fantasy points per game. Last season's leader averaged 24.5.
 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 vs ARI

His updated receiving yards pace is 2,093. He is overcoming the team's QB.
 3. Puka Nacua, WR2 @ WSH

As long as he averages 12-plus targets per game, he will thrive.
 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 vs NYJ

Underwhelming games the past two weeks, but this week he faces the Jets.
 5. Brock Purdy, QB1 vs LV

Comes off the bye week ready to blast the Raiders' defense.
 6. Joe Burrow, QB2 @ ATL

 7. Drake Maye, QB3 vs GB

 8. CeeDee Lamb, WR3 @ IND

He's not the reason they lose games. Big game coming against the feeble Colts.
 9. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR4 @ MIA

He hasn't scored a TD since Week 3, but perhaps it changes versus the Dolphins this week.
 10. Josh Allen, QB4 @ MIN

The matchup with a stingy Vikings is reason for a lower ranking than typical.
 11. Jared Goff, QB5 @ MIA

 12. Jayden Daniels, QB6 vs LAR

 13. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 vs LV

 14. Bijan Robinson, RB4 vs CIN

 15. Ja'Marr Chase, WR5 @ ATL

Incredible talent just had his first 100-yard receiving game in Week 8.
 16. Tee Higgins, WR6 @ ATL

The QB is so good that yes, the Bengals boast a pair of WR1 options.
 17. Brock Bowers, TE1 @ SF

Yep, we basically view him as a top-five wide receiver now. He's that dominant.
 18. Dak Prescott, QB7 @ IND

His rushing TD versus the Cardinals saved what would have been a disappointing fantasy effort.
 19. Patrick Mahomes, QB8 vs NYJ

Bounced back from the Seahawks debacle with 25.44 fantasy points against the Broncos.
 20. James Cook III, RB5 @ MIN

He has scored a TD in six consecutive games. The Vikings are tough, but you can't sit him.
 21. Jonathan Taylor, RB6 vs DAL

Will he still be a Colt on Sunday? Pay attention to the news. The Colts may sit him.
 22. Justin Jefferson, WR7 vs BUF

 23. Malik Nabers, WR8 @ PHI

 24. Chuba Hubbard, RB7 vs DEN

 25. Javonte Williams, RB8 @ IND

It feels like time for his second 100-yard rushing game of the season.
 26. Kyren Williams, RB9 @ WSH

Only four running backs have more points, but he is sharing more touches now.
 27. Caleb Williams, QB9 vs TB

He averages 19.5 fantasy points. The Buccaneers are defending well, but you can't sit him.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Four players whose upgraded skill sets look real
articles.description: Which players have added new dimensions to their game? Here are four who can sustain their newly-demonstrated skills.
articles.body:
Baseball analyst Ron Shandler famously posited that once a player has demonstrated a skill over a sufficiently meaningful sample, they own it. The key qualifier is that the skill must be demonstrated over a sustained period, not merely in an isolated performance or brief hot streak.

This concept applies to basketball as well. Once a player demonstrates they can effectively protect the rim over multiple months, we can assume they "own" that skill as part of their overall skill set. It was clear early in Walker Kessler's career with the Utah Jazz that he was a special rim protector -- a skill that has proved enduring.

We learn to trust what players can and cannot do on the court over time. Box scores create precedents. Past demonstrated ability deserves more weight than recent struggles because a skill can lie dormant without disappearing.

Which players are establishing new levels of expertise so far this season? Even with the sample size remaining quite small, we can begin to identify new identities around the league. With this lens in mind, let's discuss a quartet of players who have added new dimensions to their real and fantasy reputations thus far.

The prospect who was promised

Incredibly fun and prestigious player comparisons -- to the likes of Rashard Lewis and even Chris Bosh -- surfaced when Jabari Smith Jr. was evaluated during the 2022 NBA draft cycle. While those were lofty comparisons, they spoke to Smith's potential to go beyond a traditional "3-and-D" archetype and develop into a game-changing two-way force.

We're not quite at the All-Star tier for Smith, but it's becoming clear that he is taking ownership of a new level of shooting and scoring. Even though his shot diet this year is identical to last season's, he has leapt nearly 20% in scoring output thanks to appreciable spikes in shooting success. There is danger in simply trusting a hot streak. A more granular look shows Smith is finally thriving off the dribble and as a pull-up shooter, which is also showing up in his ability to initiate and finish drives.

Smith has already proven he owns a unique ability to protect the rim from an atypical position, as his career 2.5% block percentage reveals. The blend of improved shooting and scoring, along with his ability to create turnovers, has Smith positioned 20th overall on the Player Rater, just ahead of Houston Rockets teammate Alperen Sengun. Even when his outside shooting cools -- and it will -- Smith has leveled up enough to remain an impact player.

The ready rookie

Beyond being an amazing soundbite and the oldest prospect in his class, Yaxel Lendeborg was a somewhat mysterious prospect. Dominant rebounding numbers over a long college career did not necessarily indicate a dynamic offensive package.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic's 53-point explosion pushes scoring average past 40 as Lakers roll
articles.description: Luka Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points in a 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers, raising his scoring average to 40.1 PPG.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチが53得点の猛攻で平均得点40点超え、レイカーズは快進撃を続ける
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜日のブレイザーズ戦で124-118と勝利した試合で、ルカ・ドンチッチがシーズンハイの53得点を記録し、平均得点を40.1点にまで引き上げた。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Though Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and James Harden came somewhat close, no NBA player has averaged at least 40 points in a season since Wilt Chamberlain in 1962-63.

Believe it or not, Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is on pace through his first nine games of the season to reach that historic benchmark thanks to his latest 50-point explosion.

Doncic poured in a season-high 53 points to lead the Lakers to a 124-118 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on Friday. The Slovenian star is averaging a career-high 40.1 points and is captaining the NBA's No. 1 offense.

"Luka can do some things that maybe a handful, if not no one, can do in basketball," Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

Chamberlain is the only player to score more than Doncic's 361 points through his first nine games in a season. The Hall of Fame center had 472 points through nine games in 1962-63 and 455 points in the 1961-62 season, according to ESPN Research.

Chamberlain went on to average an NBA record 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 points in 1962-63. Jordan's 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 is the NBA's highest mark during the 3-point era. Harden's 36.1 points per game in 2018-19 was the most prolific scoring season of the 21st century. And Bryant's 35.4 points were the most by a Lakers player since the NBA/ABA merger in 1976.

Can Doncic, whose career high for a season is 33.9 points per game with the 2023-24 Dallas Mavericks, join Chamberlain in averaging at least 40 points?

"It's obviously a long season," Doncic said. "We're 10 games in. We've got 72 left. As long as we're winning, I'm good. I got [the shots] up today, I'm not going to lie. Hopefully, it continues, but you never know."

Doncic, 27, is taking full advantage of his new role as the undisputed face of the Lakers after LeBron James' offseason departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. Entering Friday, Doncic was leading the league in scoring, shot attempts, 3-point attempts, free throw attempts, usage rate, player efficiency rating and win shares.

Against the Blazers, Doncic exceeded 40 points for the sixth time this season and topped 50 for the second time. He ranks tied for 10th all time with 11 career games of scoring at least 50 points and is fifth among active players, trailing only Harden, Stephen Curry, Damian Lillard and James.

Doncic, whose 62-foot heave at the halftime buzzer keyed Friday's comeback win, joined Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan as the only Lakers to score at least 40 points in four consecutive games.

"[Doncic] is the MVP right now," Blazers coach Micah Nori said during his pregame comments. "Hands down."

articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs (6-2, fourth in the Western Conference) vs. Portland Trail Blazers (6-2, fifth in the Western Conference)


              Portland, Oregon; Saturday, 10 p.m. EST


              LINE: Spurs -3.5; over/under is 228.5


              BOTTOM LINE: San Antonio visits the Portland Trail Blazers after Victor Wembanyama's 52-point game in the Spurs' 112-111 win over the Dallas Mavericks.


              Portland went 42-40 overall and 29-23 in Western Conference games a season ago. The Trail Blazers gave up 115.8 points per game while committing 19.9 fouls last season.
